source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Look for pain mainly with joint use, brief stiffness after rest, and a predominantly degenerative pattern without persistent synovitis.","B":"Look for symmetric inflammatory small-joint involvement with morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes and possible fatigue or low-grade fever.","C":"Look for symptoms confined to weight-bearing joints with short morning stiffness and mechanical pain as the dominant pattern.","D":"Look for arthritis limited to older adults with no autoimmune inflammation or extra-articular features as the defining pattern."}}
source_row.rationale: NIAMS describes RA as a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that often affects joints symmetrically, especially wrists/hands/feet, with morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes and possible fatigue or fever.

source_row.stem: A client has symmetric pain and swelling in both hands with prolonged morning stiffness. Which finding is more characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis than osteoarthritis?
